subject.title: [Feature] Pre-response enforcement hooks (hard gates) for mandatory tool-call / policy rules

question: Should OpenClaw add a versioned core/plugin response-gate API for final-answer delivery, and what fail-closed or HITL semantics should it expose?
rationale: This cannot be safely decided by automation because it changes the security boundary for final output delivery, plugin trust, config/default behavior, native harness relay behavior, and audit semantics.

options.title: Design a versioned response-gate seam
options.body: Define the core ledger, validator, retry/fallback, HITL, audit, and plugin API contract before implementation; domain-specific policies can then live in plugins.

options.title: Keep only plugin/tool-side enforcement
options.body: Continue relying on pre-tool hooks, message hooks, and external plugins, accepting that OpenClaw core still cannot prove mandatory validators passed before response delivery.

options.title: Reject core response gating for now
options.body: Close the direction as out of scope and point regulated-policy users to external tooling, at the cost of leaving the reported core runtime gap unresolved.

recommendation.title: Design a versioned response-gate seam
recommendation.body: Define the core ledger, validator, retry/fallback, HITL, audit, and plugin API contract before implementation; domain-specific policies can then live in plugins.

likelyOwner.reason: The missing seam is closest to the plugin hook/API work introduced around before_agent_finalize.
